'''Shamrock Rovers Football Club''' are an Irish professional [[Association football|football]] club based in the [[South Dublin]] suburb of [[Tallaght]]. The club's senior team competes in the [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] and it is [[List of football clubs by competitive honours won|the most successful club]] in the [[Republic of Ireland football league system|Republic of Ireland]].<ref name="Shamrock Rovers Club Information">{{cite web|url=http://www.airtricityleague.com/index.php/clubs/premier-division/shamrock-rvs/club-information |title=Shamrock Rovers Club Information |publisher=League of Ireland |access-date=2 February 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100304135945/http://www.airtricityleague.com/index.php/clubs/premier-division/shamrock-rvs/club-information |archive-date=4 March 2010 }}</ref> The club has won the [[League of Ireland]] title a record 22 times and the [[FAI Cup]] a record 26 times.<ref name="shamrockrovers1">{{cite web|url=http://www.shamrockrovers.ie/about/honours |title=Roll of Honour |publisher=Shamrock Rovers Football Club |access-date=2 February 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090317095444/http://www.shamrockrovers.ie/about/honours |archive-date=17 March 2009 }}</ref> Shamrock Rovers have supplied more players to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team]] (64) than any other club. In All-Ireland competitions, such as the [[Dublin and Belfast Inter-city Cup|Intercity Cup]], they hold the record for winning the most titles, having won seven cups overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://home.online.no/~smogols/ifcp/archive/allirelandarchive/allirelandpastwinners.htm |title=Irish Football Club Project – North vs. South – Past Winners |access-date=13 April 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090415085227/http://home.online.no/~smogols/ifcp/archive/allirelandarchive/allirelandpastwinners.htm |archive-date=15 April 2009 }}</ref>

The club was founded in [[Ringsend]], [[Dublin]], in 1899.<ref name="shamrockrovers2">{{cite web|url=http://www.shamrockrovers.ie/history/history|title=A Brief History of Shamrock Rovers by Robert Goggins|publisher=Shamrock Rovers Football Club|access-date=2 February 2009|archive-date=21 February 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110221043440/http://www.shamrockrovers.ie/history/history|url-status=live}}</ref> They won the League title at the first attempt in the [[1922–23 League of Ireland|1922–23 season]] and established themselves as the Republic of Ireland's most successful club by 1949, winning 44 major trophies. During the 1950s, the club won three League titles and two FAI Cups and became the first Irish team to compete in [[Uefa#Club|European]] competition,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fai.ie/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=225&Itemid=227|title=FAI History: 1930 – 1959|publisher=FAI|date=5 June 2009|access-date=26 January 2010|archive-date=22 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322023809/http://www.fai.ie/index.php?id=225&itemid=227&option=com_content&view=article|url-status=live}}</ref> playing in the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] in 1957.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2008/0128/shamrockrovers.html?rss |title=Rovers invited to Munich commemoration |publisher=RTÉ Sport |access-date=2 February 2009 |date=28 January 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118055806/http://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2008/0128/shamrockrovers.html?rss |archive-date=18 January 2012 }}</ref> They followed this by winning a record six FAI Cups in succession in the 1960s, when they were also one of the European club teams that spent the summer of 1967 in the United States, founding the [[United Soccer Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sover.net/~spectrum/year/1967.html|title=The Year in American Soccer – 1967|access-date=2 February 2009|archive-date=2 November 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081102062256/http://www.sover.net/~spectrum/year/1967.html|url-status=live}}</ref> They won the first of four League titles in a row in [[League of Ireland 1983–84|1983–84]], after a long decline. The club played at [[Glenmalure Park]] from 1926 to 1987 when the owners controversially sold the stadium to [[Real estate development|property developers]]. Shamrock Rovers spent the next 22 years playing [[Home (sports)|home]] games at various venues around Dublin and on occasions, Ireland. They moved into [[Tallaght Stadium]] prior to the start of the [[2009 League of Ireland|2009 season]] after years of delays and legal disputes, during which time the club's supporters saved them from extinction.

Shamrock Rovers wore green and white striped jerseys until 1926 when they adopted the green and white hooped strip that they have worn ever since. Their club badge has featured a football and a [[Shamrock (Irish symbol)|shamrock]] throughout their history. The club has a relatively large support base and shares an intense rivalry with [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] and [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]]. On 25 August 2011, Rovers became the first Irish side to reach the group stages of either of the top two European competitions by beating [[FK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] in the play-off round of the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brave battlers reach the group stage|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01f4-0e7960519d79-7424fb2281c3-1000--brave-battlers-reach-the-group-stage/|publisher=UEFA|access-date=26 August 2011|date=25 August 2011|archive-date=3 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003063620/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=1668085.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2011/0825/shamrockrovers_partizan1.html |title=Partizan 1–2 Shamrock Rovers (agg 2–3) |date=25 August 2011 |work=RTÉ Sport |access-date=30 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111214043820/http://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2011/0825/shamrockrovers_partizan1.html |archive-date=14 December 2011 }}</ref> During the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League|2024–25 season]], Shamrock Rovers became the first Irish side to qualify for the knockout stages of a European tournament as they advanced past the league phase of the [[UEFA Conference League]]."}}
